answer: An apothecary on a hill lane gives each agent one numbered clay pot on a shelf. The agent plants a single kernel in the pot, seals the rim with violet wax, and tends it until saffron threads bloom, then dries the threads in a numbered tray. The apothecary weighs the dried threads against the weight written on the pot and melts any pot whose wax was broken or whose threads fall short. A thousand fake names need a thousand pots tended daily through a full season, each with its own wax seal and its own weighed tray.
